subject: Production: Harmonia inference error/latency surge — network path impact
messages:
From: James Telford <james.telford@harmonia.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@harmonia.com
Date: 2026-07-21T07:12:00Z
Subject: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

Rishi —

We started seeing a sharp increase in inference errors and tail latency on our production traffic around 07:00 UTC. Metrics: error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~12% in 30 minutes, p95 from 450ms to 4s, p99 from 3.2s to 12.8s. Customer impact: increased checkout failures and timeouts on our mobile app.

Attached: trace_20260721.pcap (packet captures from our side), request_samples_070721.csv (sample request IDs and timestamps).

Initial ask: can you confirm whether this is a Redwood service regression or something in the network path (we're seeing a lot of 502/504 from gateway/proxy in our logs)? If you have a quick mitigation (failover to another region / dedicated pool / revert a recent routing change) we need it ASAP — we have execs on call at 10:30 UTC.

Thanks,
James
CTO (acting)
Harmonia
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: James Telford <james.telford@harmonia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T07:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

James — thanks for the heads up and the captures. We're on it.

Immediate plan (first 60 minutes):
- I will spin up a small dedicated pool and prepare an IP-based routing fallback.
- Marissa, can your team start a packet-level correlation against our egress/NAT and proxy fleets now? Look for DNS timeouts, 5xx patterns, and any peering errors.
- Vanessa, please pull the last 2 hours of our VPC peering logs and firewall rule changes.
- Vivek, I'm flagging for executive awareness in case Harmonia requests an SLA credit or needs a formal exec update.

James — can you also drop a pointer to any specific request IDs that hit the 5xx so we can trace on our side? I'll update every 15 minutes.

Rishi
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T08:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

Folks — initial triage results from the first pass of correlating the pcap and our traces:
- We see repeated DNS resolution failures for several of Harmonia's resolver names, with retries that align to the p99 spikes.
- A subset of connections to our egress proxy pool returned 502/503, and those requests then hit a firewall timeout further downstream.
- NAT gateway connection table for the affected subnet shows short-lived syn-retries and conntrack churn; signs point to transient NAT exhaustion under a specific peering route.

Likely root cause hypothesis (working): a peering route flapped which pushed traffic through an overloaded path where a proxy/firewall combo began dropping/shortening TCP windows, amplifying retries and causing both DNS timeouts and 5xx responses.

Temporary mitigation suggestions we can enact in the next 30–45 minutes:
- Add an explicit route to bypass the suspect peering and force traffic through backup peering (risk: path cost increase but immediate relief).
- Increase conntrack/max-sessions on the NAT gateway for Harmonia's tenant temporarily.
- Apply a short-lived firewall rule to allow longer keepalives for the Harmonia IP block to reduce premature connection tear-down.
- Begin redirecting 30% of traffic to a small dedicated pool in a nearby region as a failover.

I've attached a filtered trace (trace_20260721.pcap) and a short CSV of impacted request IDs. I'm starting the reroute now for verification.

—Marissa
Support Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachment: trace_20260721.pcap (filtered), request_samples_070721.csv
From: James Telford <james.telford@harmonia.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@harmonia.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

Thanks Rishi — urgent please.

We need an ETA on mitigation. We have a two-way executive briefing at 10:30 UTC and our CFO/CTO will want to know whether this is a one-off or will require sustained changes/credit. Please classify this as a Sev-1 and confirm whether Redwood will run the reroute and provide an exec one-pager.

Request IDs that failed are included in the CSV. We're seeing customers retrying and compounding load.

James
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

Team — escalation accepted. High level directive: restore availability for Harmonia before 10:00 UTC and prepare a single-slide executive summary for the 10:30 call. Actions I want now: 
1) Marissa — proceed with the explicit bypass route and scale NAT/session limits as you recommended. Keep the change small and reversible.
2) Vanessa — confirm no recent firewall rule deployments in the peering path; if there were, roll back the relevant change or apply the temporary allow.
3) Rishi — coordinate with Harmonia on traffic shifting to the dedicated pool and confirm IPs/endpoint so they can immediately cutover if needed.
4) Hannah — prepare an RCA timeline and note whether the issue was due to peering instability, DNS amplification, or our proxy behavior. Include logs and the impacted regions.

I'll join the exec call from our side if the customer requests. Keep status updates every 20 minutes in this thread.

Vivek
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: James Telford <james.telford@harmonia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sharp spike in 5xx + p99 latency since 07:00 UTC

James — quick update and mitigation results: we implemented the bypass route and scaled the NAT/session limits at ~09:40 UTC, and redirected ~30% of traffic to a small dedicated pool at ~09:50 UTC. Early metrics show error rate reduced to ~1.1% and p99 latency down to ~3.4s for impacted requests.

Next steps:
- Marissa & Hannah are finalizing the one-pager and an initial RCA; we will link the doc here (https://drive.google.com/harmonia/one-pager).
- We'll keep the bypass in place for the next 6 hours while we validate stability and then plan a controlled rollback if stable.
- If Harmonia still wants permanent routing changes, we should schedule a follow-up to discuss peering topology and a longer-term peering SLA.

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for the fast collaboration — cc'ing Vivek for exec visibility. Please confirm from your side that traffic and customer flows have returned to normal.

Rishi
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachment: harmonia_mitigation_onepager.docx
